channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Held-Out Test Sets: How Large Is Large Enough
item.description: A test accuracy of 91% means little without knowing how many examples it was measured on. Here is the maths behind that intuition.

item.title: Threat Modelling for ML Systems, Not Just Accuracy
item.description: High accuracy hides where a model breaks. Threat modelling forces you to ask how it fails, for whom, and at what cost.

item.title: The ML Engineer Skill Set: Modelling Is the Smaller Half
item.description: Training a model is the easy bit. The real work is data quality, leakage-aware evaluation, and keeping the system honest after deployment.

item.title: What an MLOps Engineer Actually Does Day to Day
item.description: MLOps is less about fancy tooling and more about babysitting data, retraining models responsibly, and catching silent failures before customers do.

item.title: An MLOps Roadmap for Engineers Coming From Research
item.description: A practical MLOps roadmap for researchers moving into engineering: version control, pipelines, monitoring, and the mindset shift that ties it together.

item.title: What Fine-Tuning Actually Changes Inside a Model
item.description: Fine-tuning does not rewrite a model, it nudges it. Here is what actually shifts inside the weights and why that distinction matters for evaluation.

item.title: Fine-Tuning versus Prompt Design: A Worked Comparison
item.description: A small worked example shows where fine-tuning earns its keep and where good prompt design gets you nearly as far, faster and cheaper.

item.title: Building Your Own Evaluation Harness Before a Framework
item.description: Frameworks hide the plumbing of evaluation. Build your own harness first so you know precisely what a metric means before you trust one.

item.title: Model Evaluation Frameworks: What They Hide, Not Just Automate
item.description: Evaluation frameworks automate metrics, splitting, and reporting, but they can quietly hide leakage, weak baselines, and the wrong question entirely.

item.title: Choosing Between Classical and Deep Computer Vision
item.description: A practical guide to deciding when classical vision techniques beat deep learning, and when they don't, based on data, constraints, and honest evaluation.

item.title: Why Computer Vision Models Fail Silently on the Factory Floor
item.description: High lab accuracy hides a fragile model. On the factory floor, distribution shift and leakage-prone splits let vision systems fail quietly, with no crash to warn you.

item.title: Manufacturing Defect Detection: A Realistic Evaluation
item.description: A high accuracy score means little for rare defects. Here is how to evaluate a manufacturing vision model the way production actually needs.

item.title: What a Machine Learning Model Actually Is
item.description: A machine learning model is a function with adjustable parameters, tuned by data to reduce error. One worked example makes this concrete.

item.title: Machine Learning versus AI: Drawing the Line Properly
item.description: AI is the goal, machine learning is one method for reaching it. Confusing the two leads to bad hiring briefs and worse product decisions.

item.title: Machine Learning versus Deep Learning: A Distinction That Matters
item.description: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning, not a replacement for it. Confusing the two leads to wasted compute and weaker baselines.

item.title: Comparing Two ML Models Without Fooling Yourself
item.description: A higher accuracy score does not mean a better model. Here is a practical, honest way to test whether the difference between two models is real.

item.title: Vector Databases and RAG, Explained Simply
item.description: How embeddings and vector search let language models look things up instead of guessing, and why the plumbing matters more than the hype.

item.title: Prompt Engineering versus Fine-Tuning: Choosing the Lever
item.description: A practical guide to choosing between prompt engineering and fine-tuning, with a worked example showing when each lever actually pays off.

item.title: Named Entity Recognition: Three Approaches Compared
item.description: A practical comparison of rule-based, statistical, and neural NER, with a worked example showing where each approach wins and where it quietly fails.

item.title: Monitoring Model Drift: What to Log and When to Retrain
item.description: Drift monitoring is not a dashboard of pretty charts. It is a disciplined logging habit and a retraining trigger you can defend with evidence.
